A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable text, equations, Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–2 supporting reliable comparison. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF includes the appendix referenced in the proof and table captions; this comparison covers the supplied material.

before.justification: V1 reports original MedSAM adaptation experiments on fundus and spinal-cord MRI segmentation, including benchmark results, ablations and a qualitative refinement example.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–6 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.5 retain the same frozen MedSAM model, image-embedding refinement, DAL-CRF and foreground-entropy losses, and optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate fundus optic-cup and optic-disc segmentation and spinal-cord gray-matter MRI segmentation across the same centers. Fundus experiments retain perfect, loose and shrunken prompts; SCGM retains perfect prompts only.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain direct inference, TENT, InTEnt, GraTa, PASS, MEMO and CRF-SOD. Tables 5–6 retain the same alternative-loss comparisons and DenseCRF postprocessing comparator.

E3.justification: The ViT-B model, one-step adaptation, Dice/ASD metrics, computational evaluation, and prompt-shift ratios of 0.1 and 0.2 are unchanged. Both retain the reduced-learning-rate multistep visualization.

E4.justification: Table 5 retains K sensitivity and alternative-loss analyses; Table 6 retains component ablations and postprocessing comparison. Figure 2 presents the same iterative refinement example.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and averages across centers or prompt settings. Neither supplies seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and findings in Tables 1–6 and Figure 2 match. For example, Table 4 retains SCGM mean Dice 59.49 and ASD 11.75, while Table 1 retains 97.3 GFLOPs for the proposed method.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Proposition 1, Theorem 1, Corollary 1 and Equations 1–7 are unchanged, including the conditional-independence assumption, factorized MAP argument and displayed proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same latent-refinement contribution, avoidance of parameter updates and forgetting, approximately 3% Dice improvement claim, and approximately sevenfold computational reduction claim.

C2.justification: The explanations involving latent fidelity, sufficient statistics and foreground-entropy regularization are unchanged. Interpretations of baseline behavior and qualifications concerning prompt shifts and challenging SCGM segmentation are also retained.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same official MedSAM ViT-B checkpoints/code, Adam optimization, RoI-dependent learning rate and loss weighting, K=4 and entropy threshold 0.95. No implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 retain the same research positioning and novelty discussion. The same 33 reference entries appear in both versions.

P1.justification: V2 abbreviates the affiliations, removing departmental details, and identifies Haoliang Li as corresponding author. The scientific prose and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The compact author block shifts first-page material and causes subsequent text reflow; printed page numbers are removed. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–6 retain their designs, captions and content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds corresponding-author identification while abbreviating affiliations and removing printed page numbers. These limited editorial and layout changes leave the scientific argument, experimental evidence and reproducibility information unchanged, with no meaningful net effect on overall paper quality.
